title: Redemption
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Redemption means that Christ purchases sinners out of bondage by the price of His blood. Believers are not rescued cheaply; they are bought by the costly saving work of Jesus.
summary: Redemption means that Christ purchases sinners out of bondage by the price of His blood. Believers are not rescued cheaply; they are bought by the costly saving work of Jesus.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Redeemer who gives His life as the ransom for many. Through His blood, sinners are freed from guilt, slavery to sin, condemnation, and the empty life they once lived.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Redemption uses the language of rescue by payment. Scripture presents sinners as enslaved to sin, under curse, and unable to free themselves. Christ comes as Redeemer.

The price of redemption is not silver or gold, but the precious blood of Christ. His sacrifice purchases freedom for His people and brings them to God.

Redemption includes deliverance from the curse of the law, release from bondage, forgiveness of sins, and belonging to God. The redeemed are not free to return to slavery; they are bought for God.

The redeemed people of Christ come from every tribe, language, people, and nation. Redemption is personal, costly, global, and worship-producing.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often want freedom without a Redeemer. They may try to break bondage through willpower, self-definition, or escape from consequences. Redemption teaches that true freedom comes through Christ’s costly rescue.

This doctrine is especially powerful for those who feel owned by addiction, shame, sin, trauma, or the past. In Christ, believers belong no longer to bondage but to the Redeemer who bought them.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as one bought by Christ. Do not return willingly to the slavery from which He redeemed you. Worship Him for the price He paid, reject the lies that say sin still owns you, and use your freedom to serve the Lord who purchased you.
